name: Diffbot
follows_en: Yes, by default (disallow and crawl-delay directives)

ips.note: The vendor page does not describe an IP list or verification method.

vendor_quote: By default Diffbot's web crawls adhere to a site’s robots.txt instructions, including the disallow and crawl-delay directives.
what_en: Diffbot documents two user agents. Diffbot is used for general, proactive web crawling for building a general search engine, so sites can be discovered and cited from the Diffbot Knowledge Graph and web search services. Diffbot-User is used for requests made on behalf of a human user browsing a URL with Diffbot software.
block_en: Diffbot says its web crawls follow robots.txt by default, including disallow and crawl-delay, and that a rule can be overridden in specific cases such as a partnership or agreement with the site. It lists Diffbot and Diffbot-User as separate user agents, and says users of its Extract and Crawlbot APIs define their own crawl parameters and can set their own User-Agent.
compare_en: Diffbot is described by its operator as similar to Googlebot and Bing, a general crawler for a search index, and the vendor says it is not used for AI training.
notes: The vendor page lists only the tokens Diffbot and Diffbot-User, not a full user-agent string, so ua holds the token. The page also says Diffbot does not crawl pages for training generative AI foundation models. job set to search from the Diffbot row; Diffbot-User (user-initiated) is mentioned but not given its own file. Old URL docs.diffbot.com/docs/does-crawl-respect-robotstxt redirects to this one.
answer_en: Diffbot documents two user agents. Diffbot crawls the web proactively for a general search engine, so sites can be discovered and cited from its Knowledge Graph. Diffbot-User fetches a URL for a person using its software. Diffbot says its crawls follow robots.txt by default, including disallow and crawl-delay.
